h1: The 5 Best Portable Patio Heaters of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Portable Patio Heaters: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 portable patio heaters scored on output, coverage, tilt safety and fuel type, from 48,000 BTU propane to infrared.
summary: The Sweetcrispy 48,000 BTU propane heater is our top pick for open patios: an 18-foot coverage diameter, a built-in side table, flame-out cutoff and tilt shutoff at 45 degrees, all on wheels. The Hykolity 50,000 BTU goes to tailgates and camps. Electric buyers should look at the DR. INFRARED, which mounts three ways, or the SereneLife for a certified, weatherproof carry-around.
intro: Patio heaters are sold by BTU, and BTU is the least useful number on the box. A tall propane tower can put out 48,000 BTU, but most of that heat rises from a mushroom-shaped reflector and warms the air above your head. What matters is how far the heat actually reaches your guests, whether the unit tips off when it is knocked, and what it takes to get it lit and moved.

We ranked five portable heaters, three propane and two electric infrared, from their listings. Propane towers give the strongest heat in open spaces and need no outlet, while infrared electric heaters give directional warmth near power. We scored output, stated coverage, safety shutoffs, mobility and fuel type. Propane heaters are for outdoor use only, in open air.

products.name: Sweetcrispy 48,000 BTU Propane Patio Heater With Wheels
products.verdict: 48,000 BTU, 18-foot coverage, a built-in table and both flame-out and tilt shutoffs, on wheels.
products.description:
The Sweetcrispy produces 48,000 BTU with an 18-foot diameter coverage for 4 to 8 people, a double-layer 304 stainless steel burner, a built-in round side table, a flame-out cutoff and a tilt shutoff beyond 45 degrees. It rolls on wheels.

It ranks first because safety and use are covered in one unit: a flame-out cutoff shuts the gas if the flame dies, and tilt protection cuts it if the heater is knocked. The built-in table is a practical extra for a drink. The NEWBULIG offers the same output with a side cutout rather than a table.

Buy it for an open patio or lawn where you roll warmth to guests. Budget for a propane tank on top of the unit, since the heater does not include fuel.

products.skipIf: You have an outlet and prefer electric heat.

products.name: Hykolity 50,000 BTU Portable Propane Patio Heater With Table
products.verdict: 50,000 BTU with a stainless burner and battery-free ignition, for patio, tailgate and camp.
products.description:
Hykolity lists 50,000 BTU, coverage of up to 200 sq ft, a stainless steel burner and a piezoelectric button ignition with no battery. It comes with wheels and a table.

It ranks second because the output is the highest of the propane group and the ignition needs no battery, which removes a common failure on cold nights. It loses to the Sweetcrispy because the listing gives no tilt or flame-out details and states coverage as an area, up to 200 sq ft, not a diameter.

Buy it if the heater will also go to tailgates and camps. The caveat is that missing safety detail, so confirm the shutoffs on the listing.
products.idealFor: Buyers who take the heater to tailgates and camps as well as the patio.
products.skipIf: You want safety shutoffs spelled out.

products.name: NEWBULIG 48,000 BTU Propane Patio Heater With Side Cutout
products.verdict: An 87 inch tower with 45 degree anti-tilt protection and a side cutout for repositioning.
products.description:
The NEWBULIG gives 48,000 BTU, 18-foot diameter coverage for 4 to 8 people, an 87 inch height, 45 degree anti-tilt and flame-out protection, and rolling wheels with a side cutout.

It ranks third because it matches the Sweetcrispy on output and safety but offers a side cutout in place of a built-in table. The 87 inch height lifts the reflector above heads, which spreads heat widely. The cutout makes it easier to grab and reposition.

Buy it if you move the heater often. The caveat is that it has no table, and a tall unit is top-heavy in wind.
products.idealFor: Buyers who reposition the heater often and want tilt protection.
products.skipIf: You want a table built in.

products.name: DR. INFRARED 1500W Portable Infrared Patio Heater
products.verdict: A 900, 1200 or 1500W infrared heater with a weighted base, three mounting modes and a 12 hour timer.
products.description:
DR. INFRARED has three power settings of 900, 1200 and 1500W, a weighted base with easy-roll wheels, three-way mounting as freestanding, wall or ceiling, and a remote with a 12 hour timer.

It ranks fourth because electric infrared heats people and objects directly and warms a small zone, so it cannot match a 48,000 BTU propane tower for an open lawn. Its strengths are no fuel, no flame and flexible mounting. The weighted base resists tipping.

Buy it for a porch or deck near power where flame-free warmth is preferred. The caveat is the zone size, since 1500W warms a seat or two.
products.idealFor: Porches and decks near power where flame-free warmth is preferred.
products.skipIf: You heat an open lawn with no outlet.

products.name: SereneLife 900W Infrared Outdoor Electric Patio Heater
products.verdict: A 900W infrared heater, IP65 rated and ETL certified, 37.4 inches tall with a remote.
products.description:
SereneLife is a 900W infrared electric heater with an IP65 rating, ETL certification, a 37.4 inch height and a remote.

It ranks last because 900W is the lowest power here, and at 37.4 inches it is a table-height heater. The IP65 rating means it resists dust and water jets, and ETL certification gives a safety listing that some cheaper heaters lack. Against the DR. INFRARED, it offers less power and fewer mounting options.

Buy it for one or two people on a covered patio. The caveat is the limited output, so it is a spot warmer rather than an area heater.
products.idealFor: One or two people who want a weatherproof, certified carry-around heater.
products.skipIf: You need to heat several people or an open space.

whatMatters.detail: BTU is raw heat output, but the coverage figure tells you how far that heat actually reaches. A 48,000 BTU tower covers an 18-foot diameter, while a claim of 200 sq ft describes area. Look for a stated diameter or area, and remember wind and cold air shrink real coverage well below the stated number.

Tilt protection cuts the gas if the heater is knocked past a set angle, and flame-out protection cuts it if the flame dies. Both prevent a fuel leak. Look for a named tilt angle, such as 45 degrees, and a flame-out cutoff on the listing, and never use a propane heater under a cover or indoors.

Propane towers give strong heat with no outlet but need a tank and open air. Electric infrared heaters need power but have no flame, so they suit covered porches. Choose by where you will use it and whether an outlet is nearby, and match output to the number of people you want to warm.

A tall tower tips more easily and a short base needs weight to stay put. Wheels make a heavy unit easy to move, while a weighted base resists tipping. Look for wheels, a stated height and a base design on the listing, and keep the heater on a level, non-flammable surface.

Piezoelectric ignition lights the burner with a button and needs no battery, which is more reliable in cold weather than battery-powered igniters. Electric models offer remotes and timers. Look for the ignition type on propane units and a timer on electric ones, and keep a lighter nearby as a backup.

faq.q: Can I use a propane heater on a covered patio?
faq.a: Do not. Propane heaters such as the Sweetcrispy, Hykolity and NEWBULIG are for open-air use, because enclosed spaces risk carbon monoxide. Under a cover, the DR. INFRARED or SereneLife electric infrared heaters are the safer options.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying on BTU alone. The Hykolity's 50,000 BTU sounds strongest, but coverage and safety matter more. The Sweetcrispy lists tilt and flame-out protection, and the NEWBULIG a 45 degree anti-tilt.

faq.q: Is infrared electric worth it over propane?
faq.a: For small spaces, yes. The DR. INFRARED has no fuel and mounts on a wall or ceiling, but a 1500W element warms a small zone. For a large lawn, a propane tower is stronger.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Assemble on level ground, connect a full propane tank, check for leaks with soapy water and light it. Keep it away from walls and awnings. For the Hykolity, use the button ignition.

faq.q: How do I look after it?
faq.a: Disconnect the tank, wipe the surfaces and cover the heater when idle. Check hoses and burner screens each season. Store electric models like the SereneLife dry, despite the IP65 rating.
Keep a safe distance from the reflector and follow the manual. The 18-foot diameter coverage on the Sweetcrispy suits 4 to 8 people around it. Never place chairs against the heater.

finalTake: Buy the Sweetcrispy if you heat an open patio: 48,000 BTU, 18-foot coverage and both safety shutoffs make it the best-equipped propane tower. The Hykolity suits tailgating, and the NEWBULIG suits people who move the heater often. Pick the DR. INFRARED for a covered deck near power, and use propane outdoors only.
